part.text:
All 17 tests pass and `go vet` is clean. The refactoring is complete. ## What I did Rewrote `markdown.go` per the spec in `.docs/instructions.md` (a refactoring exercise — the original already passed, the goal is readability). The old code scanned the document one character at a time inside an infinite `for {}` loop, juggling five pieces of state (`header`, `list`, `listOpened`, `he`, `pos`) and using tricks like incrementing-then-decrementing the header level to detect `#` inside header text. The new implementation processes the document **line by line**, which matches how markdown is actually written: - `Render` — splits into lines; a line starting with `* ` is a list item (opening/closing `
    ` as needed), a line starting with `#` is a header, anything else is a `

    ` paragraph. - `applyEmphasis` — converts the first `__...__` and `_..._` pairs to ``/``, exactly as the original did (one pair of each, globally). - `renderHeader` — counts the leading `#` run; 7 or more is not a valid level and stays literal paragraph text; otherwise emits `...`. - `isHeader` / `isListItem` — small predicate helpers for the line scan. Behavior preserved for all test cases, including the tricky ones: `#`/`*` appearing inside header, list-item, and paragraph text are treated as literals, and lists close properly when followed by a paragraph. No changes to `markdown_test.go`, `cases_test.go`, or any other file.
